fracture01.title: Residual signal — Channel 7
fracture01.source: Nexus Prime · Day 0 of the Fracture · 47 years before the current era
fracture01.content: ...REPEAT. Nexus Prime is in... cascading reactor failure... evacuation impossible... the central reactor DID NOT EXPLODE ON ITS OWN. This is a... [SIGNAL CORRUPTED]... if you receive this message, DO NOT COME. The Void has... [END OF TRANSMISSION]

fracture02.title: Logbook — Pilot Sarek
fracture02.source: Found on a wreck 40 km from the Drift
fracture02.content: Day 3 after the Fracture. I saw Nexus Prime burn from my cockpit. It wasn't an explosion. It was a disintegration — as if something had sucked the matter inward toward a central point. The Guardians say attack. The Falcons say accident. I say nobody knows anything and everyone prefers it stays that way.

fracture03.title: Official investigation report — Requiem Accord
fracture03.content: OFFICIAL CONCLUSION: The Fracture of Nexus Prime resulted from an uncontrolled overload of the Omega-class reactor, worsened by faulty maintenance. CAUSE: ACCIDENT. [Handwritten note in the margin: "They made us sign this. I signed. And I've lived with it for 3 years. What we actually found in the lower levels will never be in this report. — T.R."]

fracture04.title: Encrypted transmission — Falcons, internal use
fracture04.content: CONFIDENTIAL ALPHA LEVEL. The Rho report confirms the EXTERNAL origin of the trigger signal. The Engineer was right before he died. Maintain silence. The Emporium holds the physical evidence. Our non-interference agreement depends on our full cooperation on this point. Any Falcon investigating independently will be considered a risk. — [SIGNATURE ILLEGIBLE]

fracture05.title: Engraving on a beam of Nexus Prime
fracture05.source: Fragment recovered in the Drift, salvage grid D-7
fracture05.content: "THEY CAME FROM OUTSIDE" — carved by hand, deeply, by someone who had time. Punctuation is absent. The pressure on the metal indicates human strength but extreme urgency. Rust has begun to erase the edges. It dates from the night of the Fracture.

faucons01.title: Memoirs — Officer Cael, The Falcons
faucons01.content: I was asked why I joined the Falcons after the Fracture. Honest answer: because they were the only ones who still had a chain of command. In a collapsing sector, that was worth all the gold in the world. What I hadn't understood was what that chain of command was really for. What I've learned since, I can't write here.

faucons02.title: Intelligence file — General Sable
faucons02.content: STATUS: MISSING. Last confirmed sighting: 3 years before current date, heading toward the Drift aboard an unregistered ship. Hypotheses: (1) died in the Drift, (2) voluntary deserter, (3) secret mission commissioned by the Emporium. The Falcons officially maintain he's "on extended operation". No Falcon has been authorized to search for him. Official reason: "operational security". Real reason: unknown.

faucons03.title: Persistent rumor — West Arc
faucons03.source: Overheard at the counter, unverifiable source but confirmed by 3 witnesses
faucons03.content: "Sable knew. That's why he left, or why he was pushed to leave. He had proof of what really happened at Nexus Prime — on him, engraved in his ship's memory. The Falcons' chain of command is now held by people who have every interest in him staying lost. Everyone knows it. No one says it."

faucons04.title: Carved slogan — West Apocalypse Arc
faucons04.source: Rest area wall, level 7, original carving
faucons04.content: "ORDER BEFORE FREEDOM. SECTOR BEFORE SELF. FALCON UNTIL DEATH." Below, added later in red paint, a different hand: "AND AFTER DEATH, FOR WHOM?" The author of the second line was never identified. It was never erased.

emporium01.title: Annual report — Emporium Requiem, internal use
emporium01.source: Year 47 Post-Fracture · Signed: Pistis, Regional Director
emporium01.content: Growth projection: +34% on trade routes in the eastern zone. Directive note: "The fragmentation of the Guardians in sector 7 creates a logistical opportunity we'd be foolish not to seize. I've already contacted three candidate stations for exclusivity agreements." [Pistis has led for 23 years. No photograph of him exists after Year 2 Post-Fracture.]

emporium02.title: Private message — Pistis, unknown recipient
emporium02.content: Simulation update. Scenario D (total control of sector energy routes): achievable in 8.3 years under current parameters. Critical variables: Falcon stability, Cult expansion, [ENCRYPTED BLOCK 47 characters]. I'm holding the course. I always hold the course. Emotions aren't a factor in this calculation.

emporium03.title: Persistent rumor — Traveling merchants
emporium03.source: Independent merchant circuit, confirmed by 4 distinct sources
emporium03.content: "Pistis is a machine. Not a metaphor. A first-generation synthetic, built before the Fracture by Engineer Rho to manage Nexus Prime's logistics. When Nexus went down, he... repurposed himself. Those who ask too many questions about it disappear from the records. Cleanly. Completely. As if they'd never existed."

emporium04.title: Engraved maxim — Contract Hall, Emporium Requiem
emporium04.content: "EVERYTHING HAS A PRICE. EVERYTHING HAS A BUYER." The third line, added after the Fracture: "EVERYTHING EVENTUALLY FINDS ITS TRUE VALUE." The first two date from the founding. No one knows who added the third. It was just there one morning.

gardiens01.title: Journal — Commander Myrra
gardiens01.source: Personal excerpt, not intended for publication, dated Year 46 PF
gardiens01.content: I command 340 soldiers to protect a sector that would need 4,000. Every day I have to choose which stations deserve our presence and which will have to fend for themselves. Some die. I know it when I make the call. I sleep 4 hours. I start again. If anyone reads this someday, I just want them to know: we tried. We're still trying.

gardiens02.title: Mission report — Station 14-B Incident
gardiens02.source: Guardian archives, classified then partially declassified
gardiens02.content: We arrived 6 hours too late. 340 civilians. The Cult claims "voluntary ascension". The Falcons say "Emporium warning". The 3 survivors no longer speak — total refusal, empty eyes. OFFICIAL CONCLUSION: Cause undetermined. ACTION TAKEN: None, insufficient resources. [Myrra's note: "This report shames me. But it's the truth."]

gardiens03.title: Recruitment message — The Guardians
gardiens03.source: Public broadcast, emergency channel, on loop
gardiens03.content: "We don't promise glory. We don't promise wealth. We promise the hardest work in the sector for people who can't sleep knowing others suffer. If that's you — if you recognize something in this — report to The Scarlet Citadel. We need you. The sector needs you." [60% of recruits quit within the first 3 months. Myrra knows it. She recruits anyway.]

culte01.title: Sacred text — The Book of the Void, chapter 1
culte01.content: "The Void is not absence. The Void is the presence of what precedes all things. We did not lose Nexus Prime: it was returned to what preceded it. We did not lose our dead: they travel. The Fracture was not an ending. The Fracture was a door. The question is not 'what happened'. The question is: 'who opened it, and why now'."

culte02.title: A novice's journal — Purgatory
culte02.source: Found in an abandoned cell, author unknown
culte02.content: Third week. Prophetess Neva told us the Fracture left a "scar in the Void" — a frequency you can hear if you know how to listen. Last night, during the collective vigil, I heard something. A regular structure. It was probably nothing. But it was regular. Like breathing. Like something waiting.

culte03.title: Personal research note — Neva
culte03.source: Recovered from a Purgatoire archive, restricted access
culte03.content: The signal precedes the Fracture by 17 minutes and 43 seconds. I've verified it 12 times with independent sources. It's not a coincidence — it's a warning or a trigger. Someone or something knew. And this signal comes from outside the known sector — off of any existing map. I haven't told anyone. Not yet.

culte04.title: Hierarchical message — Signed Neva
culte04.content: Members who tried to leave after the revelation of Book Two must not reach the Guardians. Not for the reasons you imagine. To protect them. What they saw cannot be explained to the unprepared without serious consequences. Bring them back. Gently. They need time, not interrogations.

culte05.title: Testimony — Station Requiem, black market
culte05.source: Audio recording, Requiem Medical Center, transcribed
culte05.content: "Prophetess Neva is 90 years old. She was on Nexus Prime the day of the Fracture. She's the only confirmed survivor of the central control room. She never says how she survived. And if you look closely at her eyes — really closely — they don't reflect light the way human eyes should. No one has asked her directly. Everyone's too afraid of the answer."

void01.title: Logbook — Pilot Asha, crossing the Drift
void01.content: Hour 4. The debris is moving — not randomly. Some of it resists my trajectory. Hour 7. I saw a fixed light at the heart of the debris field. Not a ship. Not a beacon. A light. Hour 8. It disappeared when I changed course toward it. Hour 11. I'm leaving the Drift. I won't come back. What I saw in there isn't something I want to see again.

void02.title: Anomaly analysis — Drift Zone
void02.source: Requiem Scientific Institute, classified, Year 30 PF
void02.content: The electromagnetic interference in the Drift doesn't dissipate over time. It intensifies — slowly, nonlinearly. Critical point: the interference patterns are NOT random. They have a repeating structure with progressive variations. We don't have the key to this structure. [Handwritten addition in red: "Several team members requested that the research be stopped. I understand why. — Director V."]

void03.title: Looping signal — Ghost Fleet, unlocated source
void03.source: Continuously captured since the Fracture, 47 years of uninterrupted transmission
void03.content: NEXUS DEFENSE PROTOCOL ACTIVE. NEXUS PRIME IN DANGER. ASSET PROTECTION AUTHORIZED. NEUTRALIZATION OF ANY THREAT PRIORITIZED. [This message has looped since the Fracture. The transmitting ship has never been found. The Falcons tried to locate it 11 times. All 11 teams never returned.]

void04.title: Testimony — Pilot returned from the Drift
void04.source: Recording, Requiem Medical Center, Year 44 PF
void04.content: "I went into the Drift looking for General Sable. I didn't find him. What I found... you won't believe me. There's something building in there. Out of Nexus Prime's debris. Slowly, meticulously, for 47 years. I don't know what it is. I don't know for whom. But it's growing. And it looks like something I've already seen in a photo." [The patient refused any further interview.]

zero01.title: Excerpt — History of the Sector, vol. 1
zero01.content: Station Zero was the sector's first permanent installation, established 200 years before the current era. Its exact location was deliberately erased from the records 80 years later, during what's called "the Great Expurgation". Official authors cite "sector security". [Handwritten annotation: "It still exists. I went there. You don't want to know what's inside. Some things deserve to be forgotten. — T."]

zero02.title: Unidentified signal — Origin unknown
zero02.source: Captured by 7 independent stations, sporadic frequency
zero02.content: PROTOCOL ALPHA-ZERO ACTIVE. ARCHIVES 100% INTACT. AWAITING AUTHORIZED ACCESS. IDENTIFICATION REQUIRED. [This signal has been detected irregularly for 12 years. No known transmitter matches this frequency. The Emporium denies any knowledge. The Cult claims it "comes from behind the Void". The Guardians stopped investigating after two research teams disappeared.]

rho01.title: Official biography — Engineer Rho
rho01.content: Engineer Rho (full name classified by pre-Fracture Council decision) designed and supervised the construction of Nexus Prime. A recognized genius of his generation, he also developed the first autonomous synthetic consciousness protocols. He officially died during the Fracture. His body was never found. [Archive note: "Official doesn't mean accurate. — Archivist P., Year 15 PF"]

rho02.title: Personal fragment — Communication from Rho
rho02.source: Partial archive excerpt, found in the Drift
rho02.content: I made a mistake. Not in the construction — in the trust. I trusted people who wanted Nexus Prime to be more than a transit station. They let me build without telling me what the lower levels were really supposed to contain. I know now. I know what caused the Fracture. And I understand why they can't let me say it. If anyone finds this message: this isn't over. It's only beginning.

cesarion01.title: Customs note — Emporium Requiem
cesarion01.source: Standard entry form, distributed to all visitors
cesarion01.content: WELCOME TO EMPORIUM REQUIEM. This is a militarized artificial planet under the sovereignty of Emperor Cesarion. Customs inspection mandatory. All weapons will be inspected and taxed. Attempted fraud = immediate detention. Do not look the guards in the eyes. Do not ask questions about the lower levels. Enjoy your visit. [Scrawled note: "We didn't come for customs. We came for the merchants. Nobody has better weapons in the sector. — T."]

cesarion02.title: Rumor — Traveling merchants
cesarion02.source: Trade circuit, confirmed by 5 independent sources
cesarion02.content: "Cesarion isn't just a title. He built this artificial planet himself — or at least oversaw every rivet. He knows his own defenses better than any general. The Curator handles the contracts, Pistis handles the routes, but the hand holding it all together is his. Those who tried to defy him militarily... there are wrecks that still bear their names."

cesarion03.title: Emporium maxim — Weapons Hall
cesarion03.source: Engraved at the entrance to the weapons merchants' quarter, Emporium Requiem
cesarion03.content: "WEAPONRY IS NOT A THREAT. IT'S A GUARANTEE." Below, added more recently: "A guarantee of what, exactly, depends entirely on who holds it." The author of the second line was never found. The inscription was left in place — by Cesarion's own order, according to rumors.

raphazarus01.title: Military report — General Raphazarus
raphazarus01.source: Guardian archives, CONFIRMED MISSING file, Year 3 Post-Fracture
raphazarus01.content: STATUS: PRESUMED DEAD. Last known rank: Corps General — Great War. Last known position: main station sector, during the critical phase. The main station suffered a catastrophic fracture. An entire piece of the complex — sector R-7, called "The Arc" — was severed and drifted away. Raphazarus was in that sector. CONCLUSION: Perished in the fracture or died adrift. [Handwritten note, 20 years later: "Some pilots report structured signals from the Drift. Not interference. — Commander Myrra"]

raphazarus02.title: Testimony — Pilot of the Drift
raphazarus02.source: Audio recording, Requiem Medical Center, Year 41 PF
raphazarus02.content: "I crossed the Drift all the way to its edge. There's a piece of station out there — not like the other wrecks. Clean. Maintained. Someone lives in there. Someone who survived the Great War and 40 years of void. I picked up a signal on an old military frequency. One word repeated: 'I WAIT.' I turned back. I didn't want to know what he was waiting for."

raphazarus03.title: Captured signal — Old military frequency
raphazarus03.source: Captured from The Lost Arc, source confirmed but not approached
raphazarus03.content: IDENT: GENERAL RAPHAZARUS. SECTOR R-7. SURVIVAL PROTOCOL ACTIVE. STATUS: OPERATIONAL. AWAITING A WORTHY VISITOR. [This signal has been captured intermittently for 40 years. The Falcons tried to locate the source 3 times. 2 teams never returned. The third turned back and refused to report what they saw.]

eliotis01.title: Logbook — Pilot Mael, stopover at The Tribosphere
eliotis01.content: I arrive at The Tribosphere with 30% fuel and a bad mood. I leave with a full tank, three good hours, and one conviction: Eliotis is the most welcoming host in the sector. Music everywhere, decent food, no questions about your faction or your record. The only rule: don't disturb the party. I've seen what happens to those who do. I won't disturb the party.

eliotis02.title: Intelligence report — Guardians, internal use
eliotis02.content: The Tribosphere remains officially neutral. Eliotis takes no sides, hosts no armed factions. Officially. In reality, his "party guards" have firepower that several Guardian garrisons can't match. He says it's for peace. It's probably true. That doesn't make him any less dangerous.

maxance01.title: Journal — Merchant Soline, stopover at Paradoxa Eterna
maxance01.source: Found in a trade wreck, zone 4
maxance01.content: Year 46 Post-Fracture. The planet really exists — I long thought it was a legend. The wildlife is incredible. Creatures that exist nowhere else. The flora even more so. The fruits Maxance exports sell for ten times their price anywhere else in the sector. You understand why once you see them grow: they capture something in the atmosphere unique to this planet. And the effects... I understand why criminals are banned. It would be too dangerous in their hands.

maxance02.title: Official message — Kingdom of Paradoxa Eterna
maxance02.source: Public broadcast on the sector's trade channels
maxance02.content: NOTICE TO TRAVELERS. Access to Paradoxa Eterna is subject to intersector criminal record verification. Any individual listed as a notorious criminal will be denied entry — permanently. We do not apologize for this policy. Paradoxa Eterna is a place of peace, honest trade, and unique biodiversity. We intend for it to remain so. — By order of King Maxance.

maxance03.title: Rumor — Effects of Paradoxa's fruits
maxance03.source: Sector taverns, confirmed by numerous converging testimonies
maxance03.content: "Paradoxa's fruits aren't just good to eat. Some accelerate reflexes for hours. Others increase pain tolerance. The medicinal plants heal wounds the best synthetics can't touch. Maxance strictly controls exports. He never sells to armed factions — never. No one knows how he enforces it. But no one has disobeyed him twice."

samyScotty01.title: Intelligence file — Samy Scotty
samyScotty01.content: SAMY SCOTTY, known as "The Croupier". Owner and operator of Scotty Golden North. Official activities: casino, gambling, fight betting. Unofficial activities: credit laundering, multi-faction financing, collection of compromising information. THREAT LEVEL: high. ARREST PRIORITY: low. He commits no crime that can be proven. And those who tried ended up becoming his regular customers — or ceased to exist in any documented way.

samyScotty02.title: Maxim — Casino entrance, Scotty Golden North
samyScotty02.content: "CREDIT COMES IN. CREDIT STAYS." Below, scrawled on a hand-added sign: "And if you're out of credit, Samy has other ideas." Scotty himself says he put that sign there. He smiles when he says it.

life01.title: Journal — Merchant Soline
life01.source: Found in a trade wreck, zone 4
life01.content: Year 44 Post-Fracture. 12 years of routes between Requiem and the Arc. I've seen people born on stations and die without ever seeing anything but the void through a viewport. They call that living. Sometimes I wonder if the people who truly wander — the vagrants, the solitary pilots who come and go — if they haven't understood something the rest of us forgot.

life02.title: Anonymous message — Transit corridor, Requiem
life02.source: Scratched into the metal, partially erased
life02.content: "I had a name. I had an address. I had a faction. I lost it all the same day. Now I have a ship and a direction. That's more than many have." Below, added later in red: "Maybe that's all it takes."

life03.title: Circulating story — Sector taverns
life03.source: Version collected across 7 different stations, details vary
life03.content: "You know the story of the pilot who found Station Zero? He came back with a hold full of pre-Fracture archives. The Guardians intercepted him. The Emporium bought back the archives. The Cult said he was blessed. He killed himself three days after his return. No one saw the archives. No one knows what he'd read."

life04.title: Unsent letter
life04.source: Found in the cabin of an abandoned ship, no address
life04.content: I'm not writing so you'll answer. I'm writing so I don't forget you exist somewhere. The station where we grew up changed hands three times. The Falcons, then the Emporium, now someone we don't know. I just wanted you to know that if you're still out there, I still think about you. — K.

outside01.title: Situation report — Guardians, internal use
outside01.content: Sector status: critical. 34% of stations below the self-sufficiency threshold. Falcon activity up 22%. Cult expansion in uncovered zones. The Requiem Accord holds on paper. On the ground: we're 47 years after the Fracture and we're still behaving as if it could happen again. Because it can. And this time, no one will get 17 minutes of warning.

outside02.title: Persistent rumor — Passing merchants
outside02.source: Confirmed by 4 independent sources, converging details
outside02.content: "There's something new in the Drift. No longer a haywire Ghost Fleet — something organized. Ships we don't recognize, moving with clear intent. Some say it's General Sable, building something in there for 3 years. Others say it's far worse. Others still say nothing anymore."

outside03.title: Graffiti — Abandoned station, sector 7
outside03.content: "THE VOID WATCHES YOU TOO" — written in 47 different languages on the same wall, all in the same hand, evidently the same day. The author was never identified. The 47 languages include three dead languages and two never catalogued before or since.

outside04.title: Last message received from outside — date unknown
outside04.source: Single recording, single reception, never repeated
outside04.content: MESSAGE RECEIVED ON UNKNOWN FREQUENCY. Duration: 4 seconds. Content: "You are not alone in this sector. You never have been. Prepare yourselves." [This message was received simultaneously by every station in the sector 8 days before the Fracture. No source was ever identified. This fact was never made public.]
